title: Where can you fly direct from Newcastle Airport?
author: Brogan
intro: Newcastle has more direct flights than ever this winter, after easyJet opened a base there in March 2026 and added routes to Lapland, Iceland and Copenhagen. Here's where you can fly, sorted by the kind of trip you want.
seo_title: Where can you fly direct from Newcastle Airport?
seo_description: Direct flights from Newcastle Airport for winter 2026/27: new easyJet routes to Rovaniemi, Reykjavik and Copenhagen, Jet2 winter sun and ski, and Dubai.

sections.heading: Newcastle at a glance
sections.text:
Newcastle International is the main airport for the North East. Jet2 has the biggest holiday network, easyJet has grown fast since opening a base in March 2026, and Ryanair has three aircraft based there. For long-haul, Emirates flies to Dubai, and KLM flies to Amsterdam, which connects to hundreds of destinations worldwide.

Routes and schedules change every season. We checked this list in October 2026, but always check the airline's current timetable before planning around a flight.

sections.heading: New this winter with easyJet
sections.text:
EasyJet now sells around 31 routes from Newcastle. The new ones for winter 2026/27 are mostly twice a week:

- **[Barcelona](/destinations/barcelona):** from 25 October, Fridays and Sundays, ideal for a long weekend.
- **[Fuerteventura](/destinations/fuerteventura):** from 25 October, Thursdays and Sundays.
- **[Kraków](/destinations/krakow):** from 26 October, Mondays and Fridays.
- **[Reykjavik](/destinations/reykjavik):** from 27 October, Tuesdays and Saturdays, for northern lights trips.
- **Hurghada, Egypt:** from 27 October, for Red Sea sun in winter.
- **[Copenhagen](/destinations/copenhagen):** from 5 November, Thursdays and Sundays.
- **[Berlin](/destinations/berlin):** from 20 November, Mondays and Fridays.
- **[Rovaniemi](/destinations/rovaniemi):** from 25 November, Wednesdays and Sundays, the first easy way to reach Lapland directly from the North East.

These join easyJet routes from its base launch, including [Lisbon](/destinations/lisbon), [Nice](/destinations/nice) and [Rome](/destinations/rome).

sections.heading: Winter sun with Jet2
sections.text:
Jet2 runs the biggest winter sun programme from Newcastle. For winter 2026/27 it includes:

- **The Canaries:** [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife) (up to 11 flights a week), [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote), [Gran Canaria](/destinations/gran-canaria) and Fuerteventura. These are the warmest places in Europe in winter.
- **[Madeira](/destinations/madeira)**, for mild weather, gardens and walking.
- **Spain and Portugal:** [Malaga](/destinations/malaga), Alicante, [Palma](/destinations/mallorca) and Faro, for cooler but sunny city-and-coast trips.
- **[Malta](/destinations/malta)** and **[Paphos](/destinations/paphos)** in Cyprus.
- **Morocco:** [Marrakech](/destinations/marrakech) and Agadir.
- **[Antalya](/destinations/antalya)** in Turkey.

The Canaries take around four and a half hours from Newcastle. If you're unsure which island suits you, our [November](/destinations/where-to-go-in-november) and [January](/destinations/where-to-go-in-january) pages compare winter temperatures.

sections.heading: Skiing and the Alps
sections.text:
Jet2 flies from Newcastle to three Alpine airports for winter 2026/27, from mid-December:

- **Geneva**, for [Chamonix](/destinations/chamonix) and resorts in France and Switzerland, up to twice a week.
- **Chambéry**, weekly on Saturdays, for the big French resorts.
- **Grenoble**, for the French Alps.

Many of these work best as part of a Jet2holidays package with transfers, but flight-only seats are often sold too.

sections.heading: City breaks
sections.text:
Between easyJet, Ryanair and Jet2, there's a good choice of short city breaks:

- **Ryanair** has around 22 routes, including Dublin, Kraków, Budapest, Milan, Barcelona, Brussels Charleroi and Malta, some of them seasonal.
- **EasyJet's** new winter routes add Copenhagen and Berlin, both with Christmas markets in December.
- **KLM** flies to [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam) several times a day, which is a city break in itself or a quick connection onward.

For ideas on which cities suit a short trip, see our pick of the [best places for a 3-day city break in Europe](/blog/best-places-for-a-3-day-city-break-in-europe).

sections.heading: Long-haul from Newcastle
sections.text:
Emirates flies year-round from Newcastle to **[Dubai](/destinations/dubai)**, which takes around 7 hours. Dubai is at its best between November and March, and the Emirates network connects onward to the Maldives, Mauritius, Thailand, Australia and more.

For North America, the usual options are connecting through Amsterdam with KLM, through Dublin (where you clear US immigration before you fly), or travelling to Manchester or Edinburgh for direct transatlantic flights.

sections.heading: Getting to Newcastle Airport
sections.text:
The airport is about 7 miles north-west of the city centre, and it's one of the few UK airports with its own metro station:

- **Tyne and Wear Metro:** the green line runs from the terminal to Newcastle city centre in around 25 minutes, and on to Gateshead, Sunderland and the coast. Check first and last times if your flight is very early, as the Metro doesn't run through the night.
- **Car:** the airport is just off the A696, close to the A1. There's a charge for the drop-off area outside the terminal, so check current prices before you go.
- **Taxi:** there's a rank outside arrivals.

sections.heading: Choosing where to go
sections.text:
With this much choice, start with the season and what you want from the trip: sun, snow, a city or something in between. Our [Christmas holidays](/destinations/christmas-holidays) page covers markets, Lapland and Christmas sun, and the [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) page has more short-trip ideas.

If the family can't agree, add the Newcastle routes you like to a shared somewhere.party ideas list, give everyone points to vote with, and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Can you fly direct to Lapland from Newcastle?
faqs.answer: Yes. easyJet flies from Newcastle to Rovaniemi twice a week from 25 November 2026, on Wednesdays and Sundays.

faqs.question: Does Newcastle Airport have long-haul flights?
faqs.answer: Emirates flies year-round to Dubai, around 7 hours, with onward connections across Asia, Africa and Australia. There are no direct flights to the USA from Newcastle.

faqs.question: Which airlines fly from Newcastle Airport?
faqs.answer: The biggest are Jet2, easyJet and Ryanair, with TUI for holidays, Emirates to Dubai and KLM to Amsterdam, among others.

faqs.question: Where can you fly from Newcastle for winter sun?
faqs.answer: Jet2 flies to the Canaries, Madeira, Malta, Cyprus, Morocco, southern Spain, Portugal and Antalya, and easyJet adds Fuerteventura and Hurghada in Egypt.

faqs.question: Can you fly from Newcastle to Iceland?
faqs.answer: Yes. easyJet flies to Reykjavik twice a week from 27 October 2026, on Tuesdays and Saturdays.
